vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: customer-service-reply
Version: 2.3.2

The skill is a template generator for customer service replies (pre-sale, complaints, FAQs, etc.). The core logic in `scripts/cs.sh` is a Python script that performs simple string formatting and conditional printing based on user-provided arguments. It does not perform any network requests, file system modifications, or sensitive data access, and it lacks any signs of malicious intent or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only customer service reply/template generator whose files and runtime behavior align with its stated purpose and do not request extra credentials or perform network I/O.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included artifacts: SKILL.md, tips.md and scripts/cs.sh implement customer-service reply templates and guidance. There are no unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running scripts/cs.sh to generate replies and references tips.md for best practices. The runtime script (cs.sh) runs an embedded Python generator and prints templates; it does not read system files, access environment variables, or post data externally in the reviewed content. A pre-scan flagged unicode-control-chars in SKILL.md (possible prompt-injection attempt); the visible script code does not appear to act on such characters, but the SKILL.md should be inspected for hidden/invisible characters before automated use.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its stated purpose: a local script that generates customer service reply templates and guidance. Before installing or using it, (1) inspect the full scripts for any hidden network calls or shell executions (the visible python code prints templates and looks local-only), (2) open SKILL.md/tips.md in a hex editor or show-invisible-chars tool to verify there are no malicious unicode control characters, (3) run the script in an isolated environment (container) if you plan to execute it, and (4) ensure Python 3 is available. If you will feed real customer data (order numbers, PII) into the script, treat outputs as templates only and avoid including secrets—the skill does not request credentials, but be mindful of privacy when using customer data.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: SKILL.md contained unicode control characters that the scanner flags as possible prompt-injection. This is not required for a template generator and is unexpected; the runtime script does not appear to use them, but you should inspect the SKILL.md and tips.md files for invisible characters (e.g., U+202E, U+200B) before trusting automated processing.
